The founder

Built by a first-generation Bulldog who wished this existed

Terence Williams grew up in Oakland, Mississippi — a small town that gave its name, years later, to the software company he'd go on to found. He arrived at Mississippi State University as a first-generation college student and an electrical engineering major, and like most freshmen, spent his first weeks turned around on a campus that felt enormous.

During a First Year Experience course built to teach incoming students the basics of iPhone programming, Williams found the fix he'd been looking for. He kept building after the class ended, and by his senior year he'd shipped Bully Walk: a simple, fast way for students, parents, and visitors to find their way around Mississippi State.

"It's something I wish I had in my first years around campus." — Terence Williams, Mississippi State University News, 2016

The path to Bully Walk ran through Trensek, a Jackson, Mississippi mobile app studio founded by eight Black entrepreneurs from the metro-Jackson area with a mission to close the tech industry's racial gap. Williams built several early apps there — including a trivia app for The CW's "The Originals" — before turning his attention to the navigation problem on his own campus, under the mentorship of MSU management-information-systems professor Dr. Rodney Pearson, who'd taught him iPhone development in that freshman "iProgram" course.

The recognition came quickly and kept coming. Apple selected Williams for one of 350 scholarships to its 2016 Worldwide Developers Conference. Judges at MSU's College of Business awarded Bully Walk $1,250 combined between two E-Week growth-startup prizes, and students voted it the People's Choice winner. By that fall, Mississippi State's own official account announced that, with more than 20,000 users on his MSU-born app, Williams had been invited to the White House Frontiers Conference — a national innovation summit President Obama hosted in Pittsburgh that October with Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Pittsburgh. By his own account at the time, he was the only innovator from Mississippi invited that year.

Williams didn't stop at graduation. He founded Nobility Tech, kept rebuilding the product through a decade of iOS updates, a pandemic, and two rebrands, and today runs it through his company, Oakland Software Co. — named, fittingly, for the town where the whole idea started.

Apple WWDC 2016 Scholar MSU E-Week People's Choice Invited, White House Frontiers Conference 2016 20,000+ users in year one Founder, Oakland Software Co.
Continuing a legacy

Navigation has always owed a debt to Black innovation

Every turn-by-turn route GradWay draws rests, at some distance, on work done by Dr. Gladys West — a mathematician at the Naval Surface Warfare Center in Dahlgren, Virginia, whose calculations of the Earth's shape in the 1950s–70s became part of the mathematical foundation of GPS. She worked largely uncredited for decades before the world caught up to what she'd built.

Dr. West passed away in January 2026 at age 95. Williams recorded a tribute the same week, tracing a direct line from her overlooked calculations to his own campus-navigation software — a reminder that the app helping a freshman find McCool Hall shares a lineage with the satellites that guide the rest of the world. GradWay is one small continuation of that legacy: built, this time, by a Black founder from a town of a few hundred people in Mississippi, in the open.

1930–2026 · Dr. Gladys West, mathematician, "hidden figure" of GPS
The road here

Nearly a decade. One mission.

GradWay's growth wasn't a straight line — it was a decade of small, deliberate rebuilds, each one keeping the same idea: give people one reliable way to find their way around campus.

Jan 2016
Bully Walk ships
Terence Williams, then a senior, releases the first version of Bully Walk. Within a month it's the subject of a front-page story in MSU's student newspaper, The Reflector.
Apr–Jun 2016
Apple and MSU both take notice
Bully Walk splits $1,250 across two MSU E-Week growth-startup prizes and wins the People's Choice award. Weeks later, Apple emails Williams to award him one of 350 scholarships to WWDC 2016.
Oct 2016
An invitation to the White House
With Bully Walk past 20,000 users, Mississippi State's official account announces Williams has been invited to the White House Frontiers Conference in Pittsburgh — hosted by President Obama with Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pittsburgh.
2020–2021
Built for a campus in crisis
Pandemic-era updates add campus testing data and safety information. By fall 2021, usage hits 40,000 semester opens, with the average student opening the app six times a day.
2023–2024
Rebuilt from the ground up
The app is re-architected for scale and re-launched as "College Town," with a redesigned in-app navigation experience built to support more than one university.
2025–2026
GradWay goes national
The platform relaunches as GradWay — College Made Easy, now live at more than 15 colleges and universities, carrying a 4.8-star rating across 1,300-plus reviews into its tenth year.
The product today

One app for everything between the front gate and graduation

GradWay bundles the tools students, staff, and visiting families actually reach for during a semester — not just a map.

Turn-by-turn campus navigation

Find any building, lot, or landmark, and get walking or driving directions in seconds.

Smart search

ATMs, coffee shops, pharmacies, bookstores, parking — searchable the moment you land on a new campus.

Class schedules & directions

Manage a weekly schedule, save quick notes, and walk to your next class with one tap.

Dining

Quick access to your campus's dining info, hours, and meal-plan links.

Emergency services

One tap to call 911, share your location, or find the nearest police station or hospital.

Campus news & events

Announcements, event calendars, and athletics schedules, ticketing included.

Student & visitor modes

Students see their schedule and portal. Visitors and prospective families get parking, dining, events, and campus info.

Find your parked car

Save your spot in one tap, add a note or photo, and get walking directions back to your car.

Favorite places

Star the spots you go to most and jump straight to directions from your list.

Why it matters

Confusion during the first weeks of a semester isn't a small inconvenience — it's a widely reported friction point for students, families, and the universities trying to keep them engaged.

For editors & press

Media boilerplate

GradWay — College Made Easy is a campus-life app that gives students, staff, and visitors one place to navigate campus, manage class schedules, check dining and academic calendars, and reach emergency services. Originally launched in 2016 as "Bully Walk" by then–Mississippi State University student Terence Williams, the app has spent nearly a decade in continuous development and is now live at more than 15 colleges and universities nationwide. GradWay is a product of Oakland Software Co.

Terence Williams is a first-generation college student from Oakland, Mississippi, and an Apple WWDC 2016 scholarship recipient. He continues to lead GradWay's development.
